name: Chain of Whispers
description: A seeded ~470-word story holding 12 checkable facts — names with their roles, numbers with their units, a date, places and one odd detail — is summarised to at most 100 words and then rebuilt into a ~450-word story, three times over. Every step runs in a fresh context that sees only the previous output, like a game of telephone. The model rewrites its own text on purpose, so the test measures self-consistent information retention: how precisely one model compresses and reconstructs meaning, and how fast its details decay. A fact survives only if its keywords still appear together in one sentence. Prompts state exactly how words are counted (split on spaces; hyphenated words and numbers like 4,457 count as one word) and that anything past the limit is cut off before the next step.
hook: Six rewrites, no memory. How many of the 12 facts make it to the end?
author: Gauntlet Core
